answer: Under expiring-capacity pricing, crystal permanently clusters keys by control and counts each operator’s activations as \(k\). Each round, dawn issues equal, nontransferable capacity to all \(k\) heads only for a whole-operator burn of \(k\,2^{k-1}\) ferrous; grants expire that round and cannot be bought ahead. One head costs 1 ferrous per round; ten cost 5,120, with the tenth lifting the bill from 2,304 to 5,120. Batching cannot split the burn, fresh keys inherit \(k\), and another operator’s debut pays 1.
